How to Make a 3D-Printed Cookie Cutter and Stamp from an Image

Turn a PNG or JPG into a cookie cutter and matching embossing stamp. Edit the outline, set the size, and export free STLs or a one-plate 3MF.

Open Cookie Cutter Maker

1. Upload an image and confirm the outline

Upload a PNG or JPG, or choose Try the star sample. A transparent PNG with a clear silhouette is a good starting point. For an opaque image, adjust Brightness threshold and use Invert light and dark if needed. Select the correct detected shape, or use Edit outline or Draw new outline to define the boundary yourself.

2. Choose the finished size and stamp style

Set the cookie width or height in millimeters. The dimensions refer to the inside cutting boundary. Choose Color outlines to trace borders between solid colors, or Bold lines for artwork with distinct linework. Use Plain stamp to omit raised artwork. Adjust the emboss depth or cleanup if the details look too fine.

3. Preview the cutter, stamp, and ring

Select Confirm outline and preview. Use Show cutter, Show stamp, and Show ring handle to inspect the parts. Look for a continuous cutting edge and check that raised stamp details are where you want them. If a narrow corner disappears, increase the cookie size or smooth the outline.

4. Download, slice, and assemble

Download the one-plate 3MF or use the free individual STLs. Keep the cutter’s handling lip flat on the build plate with the cutting edge facing up. Check the cutting edge, stamp relief, and ring threads in your slicer’s layer preview. After printing, screw the ring into the back of the stamp. Use the cutter to define the shape and the stamp to add details.
